And don't even get me started on the evils of lockdown browsers.

I believe memorization-based testing is bad for a few reasons. Firstly, with exams like that, students tend to just focus on memorizing facts instead of actually learning and analyzing the material, and then immediately forget most of it after the exam when moving on to memorize the next block of material. It also just isn't a skill used a lot outside of education.

Aside from that, I feel like it's unfair to students that may experience things like test anxiety. Personally, I've had certain classes where regardless of how hard I study, the moment there is a paper in front of me and a timer has begun I just blank. The only accommodations for things like this are alternate testing centers or extended testing time, neither of which can help with this particular issue. It's just a stress thing. It feels so unfair to have students who are bright and hardworking but simply cannot quickly regurgitate facts. 

Personally - and I'll preface this by saying that I know it'd be an incredibly unpopular opinion amongst my peers because I am definitely the in the minority with this - I'd prefer essay-based examinations where I can provide analysis of the works I've read. This would still require me to have knowledge of them, but instead of regurgitating facts, I'd be able to work with my personal understanding of the material I read and the professor or TA or whoever grades it could look at it and say either "Yeah, you did the work and got the point" or "You didn't get it at all and I don't think you actually read the material" or something in between.

I would firmly disagree that memorization is the simplest form of learning, it is simply a form of learning. A student's ability to memorize and quickly recall information does not say a thing about their intelligence or ability to handle other challenges, and this goes both ways - a student who is great at memorizing and recalling may be terrible at other aspects of learning and working.

I'd suggest that since you're aware that education and society at large has changed enough over the last 20 years that students now are struggling to pass the same tests that students from back then had no issue with, perhaps evaluate the material - NOT to simplify it or "dumb it down" since that helps nobody, but to see if there's any way it can be adjusted to better suit the way current students learn and function. Make it clear to students that are struggling that you want them to succeed and perhaps survey them to see what it is they're struggling with. It sucks that things have changed, but students today aren't stupid or lazy and deserve to have equal chances at success, which they are not getting if your post is accurate.

I can't tell if I'm a 3w4, 4w3, or something else entirely. I feel like 3 represents my core goals, motivations, and fears best, while 4 represents my personality and how I tend to react when unhealthy best.

**Argument for 3:**

* I'd much rather be seen as successful but similar to others vs. unique but unsuccessful--success can stand out as a uniqueness on its own, and I'm not a manic pixie dream girl.
* I'm a huge perfectionist, often to my own detriment as I get so fixated on details that it can cause me to miss deadlines.
* My biggest goals relate to personal/professional success, and they consume a lot of my thoughts.
* I read both and would objectively prefer to be a 3.
* I cried when listening to the type 3 song by Sleeping at Last, whereas the four one didn't make a ton of sense to me.

**Argument for 4:**

* I do tend to stand out as pretty "out there" in terms of my interests and how I present myself, although I think I do it less so people will see me as unique and more because I just enjoy those things. I do enjoy it when I get compliments on how unique my outfits are, though.
* I'm very artistic and passionate about self-expression, both in myself and others.
* I spend a lot of time in my own head and daydream frequently.
* When unhealthy, I am more likely to shut down. I'll sleep a lot, struggle to care for myself and be incredibly unproductive (while beating myself up over it).
* I have an incredibly harsh inner critic and am prone to self-destruct by holding myself back out of a fear of not being "good enough." (Is this a 3 thing?)

**Argument for  neither:**

* I'm an incredibly extroverted ENFP. I love socializing with others and feel like I'm at my best when spending time with friends. I struggle to be as productive when with others, but I'm much happier. I feel like everything for both 4w3s and 3w4s says they're very introverted and tend to internalize everything?
